text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager — 5xx / elevated latency spike in eu-west-1 (eu-west-1a) across HTTP routes (elb/app/frontend). Alert: https://monitoring/redwood/alerts/ALERT-502-euw1a
carol.oncall: I'm on it. Seeing ELB error rate jump ~18% and Route53 latency up for the same region. Dashboards: http://dash/reloads -> 502 spike aligns with AZ 'a'.
ben.engineer: digging into app logs, I'm seeing a lot of 'Connection reset by peer' and a handful of EBS attach errors on instances in eu-west-1a: 
```
I/O error: AttachVolume failed: timeout
[2026-03-15T20:03:12Z] ENI detach event for eni-0abc1234
```
frank.netops: running mtr -> packet loss ~30% to IPs in eu-west-1a from multiple edges. Traceroute shows first hop inside AWS fabric with high latency. Looks like partial network isolation in AZ.
alice.sre: hypothesis: network plane in eu-west-1a is degrading causing ELB target health checks to fail and backend EBS ops to stall. Plan: 1) route traffic away from eu-west-1a using Route53 weighted failover + lower TTL, 2) put targets in eu-west-1a to draining, 3) scale healthy AZ capacity, 4) open AWS support case for ENI/EBS fabric.
carol.oncall: executing plan now. Submitting Route53 change to shift weight off AZa (temporary). Using TTL 60.
carol.oncall: Route53 change-batch (snippet):
```
{"ChangeBatch": {"Changes": [{"Action": "UPSERT", "ResourceRecordSet": {"Name": "api.redwood.example.", "Type": "A", "SetIdentifier": "eu-west-1a-traffic-shift", "Weight": 0, "TTL": 60}}]}}
```
ben.engineer: starting ASG scale-up in eu-west-1b/c and adding more capacity to target groups. Command: `aws autoscaling set-desired-capacity --auto-scaling-group-name frontend-euw1b --desired-capacity 20`
frank.netops: opened support case with AWS (case #CASE-20260315-001). Requested network fabric/EBS team. AWS status page shows "degraded networking for eu-west-1a" (link: https://status.aws.amazon.com/incidents/XYZ).
dave.support: drafting incident notification for customers. Draft: "We’re experiencing degraded performance and increased errors for requests routed to eu-west-1a. We are shifting traffic to other AZs and will update when resolved. If you see persistent errors, failover to another region or contact support." Who can give an estimate for affected customer %? :phone: 
erin.product: quick estimate from traffic dashboards: about 20–25% of global requests for some tenants are currently routed through eu-west-1a; for EU customers that prefer regional routing impact looks like 18–22% of traffic. Recommend proactive credits for top 10 customers impacted.
alice.sre: while DNS change propagates, I'm setting ELB target group attributes to deregister slow targets faster and enabling connection draining: `aws elbv2 modify-target-group-attributes --target-group-arn arn:... --attributes Key=deregistration_delay.timeout_seconds,Value=30`
ben.engineer: verified health-checks against a sample instance in eu-west-1a: `curl -v http://10.0.11.45/health` -> connection reset. Health-checks failing.
carol.oncall: Route53 weighted shift applied, ELB draining started for targets in az-a. Monitoring metrics now.
incident-bot: Update — AWS reports "issue under investigation" for networking in eu-west-1a. Link posted to case.
frank.netops: also saw EBS IO latency spikes, likely tied to host-level networking. Recommending not to detach volumes forcefully; let AWS handle.
dave.support: Sent initial customer notification to impacted list. Erin, please review the message for top-tier customers.
erin.product: Reviewed and sent. Also flagged top 5 accounts for direct outreach.
ben.engineer: traffic is shifting. 5xx rate reduced from 18% -> ~3% in last 10m. Some background jobs still failing due to EBS attach retries. Will monitor backlog.
carol.oncall: AWS posted a partial mitigation: fabric team rolled a fix to some hypervisors in eu-west-1a; we're seeing drop in packet loss. Still in monitoring.
frank.netops: remain vigilant for ENI flaps; added a CloudWatch alarm for ENI detachment rate in eu-west-1.
incident-bot: Incident status: mitigated -> partial. Auto-runbook reminder: create postmortem and customer impact summary.
carol.oncall: Handoff to night on-call in 30m. Tasks for handoff: 1) keep Route53 weights at 0 for eu-west-1a until AWS clears, 2) monitor 5xx rate, 3) validate EBS backlog drains, 4) coordinate final AWS confirmation.
noah.oncall: ack — I'll take over at 22:30 UTC and monitor for 4 hours. Please ping if anything changes. :wave: 
dave.support: Post-incident comms scheduled, credits approved pending SRE impact calc.
erin.product: Customer impact summary (short): ~18–22% of EU traffic for susceptible customers, spike lasted ~45 minutes before weighted failover, some background processing delays persisted for ~90 minutes. Recommendation: proactive credits for top 10 affected customers + blog post with root cause once postmortem done.
alice.sre: assigning postmortem owners: carol.oncall (incident lead), ben.engineer (investigation), frank.netops (network analysis), dave.support (customer comms). Will create JIRA and link to this thread.
carol.oncall: final: 5xx baseline restored, Route53 remains weighted off eu-west-1a until AWS confirms full recovery. Closing the active paging but keeping thread open for postmortem updates. :white_check_mark:
